classification_rules.DIRECTION_CHANGE: AUC > 0.5 for one checkpoint AND AUC < 0.5 for the other
classification_rules.NO_USEFUL_SIGNAL: both 95% CIs include 0.5 AND both PR-AUCs are within +/-0.03 of prevalence
classification_rules.STABLE_SIGNAL: both AUCs > 0.5 AND both bootstrap CI lower bounds > 0.5
classification_rules.DIFFERENT_STRENGTH: same direction (both AUCs > 0.5) but materially different AUC (|dAUC| >= 0.10) or CIs that do not fully exclude 0.5

measured_dynamic_range_finding.note: the recorded confidence statistic has almost no dynamic range at F2 (all 182 examples fall in one 0.1 bin) while A0 spans nearly the full probability range; this is a measured property of the recorded scores and is the reason the confidence direction is unstable

definitions.SIGNAL_CONFIRMED: at least one statistic AUC > 0.70 with CI clearly above 0.50 AND PR-AUC materially above prevalence
definitions.SIGNAL_PARTIAL: at least one statistic AUC > 0.60 with direction supported by the CI but signal not stable across both checkpoints
definitions.SIGNAL_WEAK: AUC generally 0.55-0.60, or CIs overlap substantially with 0.50, or PR-AUC improvement is small
definitions.SIGNAL_ABSENT: no statistic provides meaningful separation and results remain near random

task_15_decision_boundary.applied_tier_gate: The given definitions separate SIGNAL_CONFIRMED from SIGNAL_PARTIAL only by whether the statistic is 'not stable across both checkpoints'. The literal threshold-only clause of SIGNAL_CONFIRMED is met by the F2 statistics listed, but the signal does not survive the checkpoint comparison (A0 shows no statistic above 0.5432 and five of six A0 CIs include 0.50, while three statistics reverse direction between checkpoints), so the applied verdict is the lower tier. Both readings are reported rather than resolved silently.

stability_label_definitions.most_stable_signal: statistic with the highest worst-case AUC across the two checkpoints (min of F2/A0 AUC); STABLE_SIGNAL classifications take precedence
stability_label_definitions.smallest_checkpoint_delta_statistic: statistic with the smallest |dAUC| between checkpoints (may be small only because both are near chance)
stability_label_definitions.most_checkpoint_sensitive_signal: statistic with the largest |dAUC| between checkpoints

interpretation_boundary: No inference, no model loading, no training, no database, no retrieval was used.
No threshold was fitted and no K was searched; every statistic is evaluated threshold-free (AUC/PR-AUC) or at the already-recorded K values.
No classifier and no derived/combined score were created.
ROC-AUC and PR-AUC are ranking-quality measurements, not causal effects and not architectural evidence.
A weak or absent answerability signal measures the CURRENT extractive outputs only; it does not prove anything about a differently designed answerability component.
No statistic is declared universally superior; results are reported per checkpoint and per budget.
